To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Reflecting on the clinical encounter with a standardized patient and revisiting the patient to improve performance is an effective strategy for medical students to improve their clinical performance on a clinical examination.”

(1) offering third year medical students an optional “reflect-revisit” experience during a clinical skills exam produced a small but significant increase in their performance; and (2) students perceived the experience as enhancing patient centered practices (counselor, education) as as their own medical decisions making and clinical confidence.

1) Reflecting and revisiting a standardized patient during a clinical skills exam improved junior medical students’ clinical performance; 2) Students perceived the reflect-revisit experience as enhancing their own medical decision-making and clinical confidence as well as patient-centered practices; and 3) The reflect-revisit experience was rated positively by the vast majority of students.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether reflecting and revising the “patient” improves students’ clinical performance.
the effects of reflective practice on the performance of medical students in a clinical skills examination.
a new approach to clinical teaching that may have a significant impact on medical education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the “reflect-revisit” option improved students’ clinical performance and was perceived positively by students.
reflecting and revisiting an SP during a standardized clinical skills examination can enhance clinical performance and that this is a feasible and potentially useful educational intervention.
the reflect–re-visit experience enhances clinical performance, and students perceive the experience as valuable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reflection and revisit intervention is an effective and feasible method of improving students’ clinical skills.
the use of reflection in medical education has the potential to improve the quality of care that students deliver to their patients.
reflection is important and should be a regular part of the learning process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reflection and revisiting an SP during a standardized patient encounter is a feasible way to enhance students’ performance.
the act of reflecting can have a positive effect on students’ performance in clinical skills examinations.
students’ reflection on their performance and revisiting the patient during a SP examination may be a valuable tool in enhancing their performance and patient-centeredness.
